Population increased in Milton Keynes

The estimated population of Milton Keynes in 2024 was 305,884 usual residents, a rise of 1.9% since 2023.

This meant that Milton Keynes' rate of population change placed it among the 20 percent fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Milton Keynes increased by 6.1%.

Over this slightly longer period, Milton Keynes was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Milton Keynes

The average (median) age rose to 38 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Milton Keynes has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Milton Keynes is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Milton Keynes' population of 305,884 usual residents was made up of:

  • 66,211 people aged 0 to 15 years, (21.6%)
  • 196,168 people aged 16 to 64 years, (64.1%)
  • 43,505 people aged 65 years and over, (14.2%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Milton Keynes has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (14.2% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Milton Keynes, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Milton Keynes
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Milton Keynes, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 1,228 people (0.4%). In total, there were 3,215 births and 1,987 deaths in Milton Keynes.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 351 (0.1%). There were 15,676 people entering the area and 15,325 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Milton Keynes' population of 4,289 (1.4%) as a result of 6,524 people entering the area and 2,235 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Milton Keynes was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Milton Keynes in mid-2023 is 300,173.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 2,041 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 138 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,903 people.
